title: The 5 Fastest Signals in Your Body, Ranked (Pain Isn't in the Top 3)

scenes.text: The five fastest signals in your body, ranked. Pain doesn't even make the top three.
Number five: dull pain. The ache after a stubbed toe crawls along at about one metre a second.
scenes.label: Dull pain · ~1 m/s

scenes.text: Number four: the nerves running your gut and heartbeat. Around 10 metres a second, and you never feel them.
scenes.label: Gut and heart nerves · ~10 m/s

scenes.text: Number three: sharp pain. The first stab of a cut arrives at up to 30 metres a second. That's why a cut hurts twice.
scenes.label: Sharp pain · ~30 m/s

scenes.text: Number two: touch. Pressure on a fingertip reaches your brain at about 75 metres a second, faster than a highway car.
scenes.label: Touch · ~75 m/s

scenes.text: Number one: position sense. The nerves telling you where your limbs are run at 120 metres a second, over 400 kilometres an hour. Close your eyes, touch your nose. That's the fastest wire in you.
scenes.label: Position sense · 120 m/s

description:
The five fastest nerve signals in the human body, ranked by conduction speed.
Nerve fibres are graded by size and insulation: unmyelinated C fibres carrying dull, burning pain move at roughly 0.5 to 2 metres a second; thin autonomic B fibres run at about 3 to 15; A-delta fibres for sharp pain and cold reach 5 to 30; A-beta touch fibres 35 to 75; and the thick A-alpha fibres for muscle position and movement 80 to 120 metres a second, about 430 kilometres an hour. That gap is why a cut hurts twice: a sharp stab first, the slow ache seconds later.
Which of these surprised you most, and what should we rank next?
first_comment: Which would you have put at number one? Bonus: the slow pain fibres are also the ones that carry itch, which is why scratching feels so good. What should we rank next?
